thread:
tyler_h: Pushed an nsight + nvprof capture for the 4-GPU TP+PP run after kernel_selector_v2 rolled. Seeing p99 climb ~8-12%. Link to timeline: https://internal/trace/1926001234 :eyes:

alex_k: :eyes: grabbing it now. Quick Q — did KV prefetch go out in the same deploy?

tyler_h: yes, batching heuristic window bumped 8ms->14ms and we enabled kv_prefetch for tail micro-batches. The goal was fewer tiny batches but now overlap looks weird.

maria_g: skimmed the nvprof: allreduce start shifted earlier and there are idle gaps where compute kernels finish late. ~3-6ms idle slices on some ranks. Could be kernel selection changed kernel launch pattern.

alex_k: can you paste the custom timers you logged? also which streams are used for comm vs compute?

tyler_h: paste: 
```
[custom_timers]
forward_compute: 12.3ms
kv_prefetch: 1.1ms
allreduce_start: 12.9ms
allreduce_end: 15.4ms
kvmerge: 0.6ms
postprocess: 1.2ms
```
Not high fidelity but shows allreduce starting while compute still running.

maria_g: two hypotheses: 1) kernel_selector_v2 picked a different matmul kernel (lower occupancy / extra launches) so compute ends later; 2) batching window change altered seq distribution -> KV prefetch timing shifts and interferes with comm streams.

alex_k: micro-benchmarked kernel_selector_v2: ~5% higher kernel launch latency for small seq (<=64) on A100s. Also check whether v2 picked a split-K variant (more launches). Are we using separate comm_stream per TP shard?

tyler_h: we have a comm_stream per shard, but ordering relies on stream semantics. kernel selector might be launching kernels in a way that exposes inter-stream ordering issues.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: rolled kernel_selector_v2 to staging at 2026-03-15T10:12Z.

maria_g: actionable: enable nsight timeline 'KernelLatency' + 'Memcpy' lanes and capture CUDA API calls. That'll show cudaStreamSynchronize / events if any. Also collect nvprof cudaLaunchTime counters.

tyler_h: did the A/B:
```
cfg A (v1, kv_off): p99=48.2ms, allreduce_idle=0.8ms
cfg B (v1, kv_on): p99=47.9ms, allreduce_idle=0.9ms
cfg C (v2, kv_on): p99=52.1ms, allreduce_idle=4.4ms
```
So v2 seems to be the smoking gun.

alex_k: sounds like v2 selected a split-K algo. If it fragments matmul into multiple launches, the allreduce handoff timing changes (partial results ready earlier) causing NCCL to start earlier and then wait for remainder -> stalls. Can you diff kernel maps?

tyler_h: dumped kernel metadata: v1 chose 'sm80_fmha_v1' while v2 chose 'sm80_fmha_splitk_v3' for 512x512 matmul on seq<=64.

alex_k: split-K explains extra launches. That typically increases total latency for these small inputs and changes ordering.

maria_g: proposed mitigations:
- blacklist split-K for N<=1024 when seq<=64 in kernel_selector rules (fast fix)
- move KV prefetch to a separate dedicated stream but schedule it after forward compute to avoid interleaving with compute/comm critical path
- make batching window adaptive based on measured cudaLaunchTime and kernel latency distribution

tyler_h: filing a tiny PR to reject split-K for the small-case and will run a regression suite. Also will test forcing old kernel via env override (KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE).

sre-bot: perf-alert: p99 increased 8.4% for staging cluster (group: tp-pp) — created PERF-3241.

alex_k: once PR is up, we can hotfix to staging and re-run the captures. If that fixes, we follow-up with a more robust selection rule (cost model incorporating launch latency).

tyler_h: running the forced-old-kernel test and will post new timeline. Thanks all :thumbsup:
